## What

Parametrize the existing detector and close-guard suites over both `[non-codebase]` and
`[operator-attested]` so the alias has an explicit regression suite rather than relying on the
old tests incidentally still passing.

## Scope

Add a both-spellings case to: `tests/unit/test_det_attestation_launder.py`,
`tests/unit/test_det_measurement_provenance{,_heldout}.py`,
`tests/unit/test_attested_close_guard.py`,
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_close_guard_e2e.py`,
`tests/unit/test_a8e5_operator_attested_edge.py`.

Also cover the PLAN-TIME surfaces the parent AC names but the guard suites do not reach:
`tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py` (the `p6_ac_quality` advisory lint via
`operator_evidence_ac_gaps`) and `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` (the `decide_ops` Pass-3
`enrich_operator_attested` path). Without these, the parent's five-surface parity claim is
unproven for two of its five surfaces.

Decide and pin the near-miss policy for the new tag: `[operator_attested]` is a DELIBERATE
non-match asserted in ~15 places (ADR-0043). `[non_codebase]` and `[noncodebase]` need the
same treatment.

## Coverage ALREADY LANDED by S1 (do not duplicate)

S1 landed `tests/unit/test_non_codebase_tag_edge.py`, which already parametrizes both spellings
over the plan-time lint (`test_plan_time_lint_parity`, p6_ac_quality) and over Pass-3 enrichment
(`test_enrichment_parity`, operator_attested_ac_texts), and already pins the near-miss non-match
policy for `[non_codebase]`, `[noncodebase]`, `[non codebase]`, `[operator_attested]` and
`[codebase]` (`test_near_misses_fail_safe_to_codebase_verifiable`). The legacy underscore
near-miss is additionally pinned in `tests/unit/test_a8e5_operator_attested_edge.py:21-24,56-61`.

Those two parity surfaces and the near-miss policy are therefore PROVEN, not outstanding. This
story does not re-assert them; it extends both-spellings coverage to the guard suites S1 did not
reach.

## Scope boundary with S6

`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_ac_checkbox_precheck*.py` is OWNED BY S6, which changes the
close-guard message strings those tests assert on. This story does not touch it, so S3, S4 and
S6 are file-disjoint and may be executed in parallel. Close-gate parity for the new tag already
landed with S1 in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_non_codebase_close_exempt.py`, so nothing is
lost by the exclusion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each listed suite exercises both spellings and asserts identical outcomes.
- [ ] The laundering detector, the provenance guard, and the a8e5 edge suite each exercise both
      spellings and assert identical outcomes.
- [ ] `[non_codebase]` and `[noncodebase]` are asserted NOT to match, mirroring the existing
      `[operator_attested]` contract.
- [ ] No existing assertion was weakened to make the new cases pass.
